title.rendered: It Is for Your Good That I Go: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Jesus said it was for our good that He was going. The departure was not the loss of His presence. It was the multiplication of it across every believer.

content.rendered:
It is for your good that I go. Jesus said this knowing what waited on the other side of His leaving. Pentecost. The Spirit. A church filled with the very presence of God. The advantage is not what we would have chosen. It is far better than what we would have chosen.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, May 19, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“But very truly I tell you, it is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.”
John 16:7 (NIV)

Today’s Message

This is one of the more startling statements in the New Testament. Jesus, sitting with the disciples on the night before the cross, tells them their lives will be better when He is gone. Better not having Him at the table. Better not having Him to follow down a road. Better not seeing Him with their eyes. How could that possibly be true?

Because Jesus in flesh could only be in one place at one time. Sitting with Peter in Capernaum meant He was not also walking with John in Jerusalem. Talking with Mary at Bethany meant He was not also encouraging Andrew in Galilee. Jesus, in His earthly body, was limited by geography just like any other human being. And the disciples, even with Him nearby, could feel utterly alone the moment He stepped into another room.

But the Spirit is not limited that way. The Spirit can be in every believer at once. The Spirit can be with the missionary in a Lagos slum and the office worker in a London tower and the grandmother praying over her grandson in a village in Kenya, all at the same moment, in the same fullness. The departure of Jesus was not the loss of Christ’s presence in the world. It was the multiplication of it.

That is why Jesus said it was for our good that He was going. Not because the cross alone would secure our salvation. Not just because the empty tomb would prove His power. But because the cross and the empty tomb together would clear the way for the Spirit to come and live in His people forever. The cross opened the door. Pentecost was when He walked through it.

If you belong to Christ today, you are living on the better side of what Jesus said in John 16:7. The Spirit is with you not when you make it to a holy place but wherever you go. He is not waiting for you at church. He is in you right now. The advantage Jesus spoke of is not future. It is yours today.

Prayer

Father, thank You that the going of Jesus was not the loss of His presence. It was the opening of the way for Your Spirit to come and live in me forever. Forgive me for the moments I have wished for less than what You have given. Help me see the gift of the indwelling Spirit for the wonder that it is. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

It is for my good that Jesus went. The cross opened the way and Pentecost brought Him in. The Spirit of God lives in me right now. I am not waiting for His presence. I am walking in it. That is the advantage of which Jesus spoke. That is my reality in Christ.
